(I) It is easier to remove 2p electron than 2s electron

(II) 2p electron of B is more shielded from the nucleus by the inner core of electrons than the 2s electrons of Be.

(III) 2s electron has more penetration power than 2p electron.

(IV) atomic radius of B is more than Be (Atomic number B = 5, Be = 4)

options.content: (I), (III) and (IV)
(II), (III) and (IV)

en.explanation:
In the first ionization, Be () loses a electron while B () loses a electron.

A electron penetrates closer to the nucleus than a electron, so statement (III) is correct.

Owing to its lower penetration, the electron of B is more effectively shielded from the nucleus by the inner core of electrons than the electrons of Be, so statement (II) is correct.

The electron of B therefore feels a smaller effective nuclear charge and is easier to remove than the electron of Be, so statement (I) is correct; this is why of B is smaller than that of Be.

Atomic radius decreases across a period as the nuclear charge increases, so B (88 pm) is smaller than Be (111 pm) and statement (IV) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
